root_cause.text: The runtime suspend path calls dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0) to drop the voltage rail to MIN_SVS without first reducing the core clock frequency, leaving a mismatch between the low voltage and the still-high clock rate that causes instability when the clock is re-enabled during resume.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states: "calling dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0) drops the MMCX rail to MIN_SVS while the core clock frequency remains at its original (highest) rate... leading to a situation where the MMCX rail is at MIN_SVS but the core clock is at its highest rate... rail cannot sustain the clock rate, which may cause instability or system crash." The patch removes the dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0) call from dpu_runtime_suspend.

Author: Rajendra Nayak <quic_rjendra@quicinc.com>

    drm/msm/dpu: Use OPP API to set clk/perf state
    
    On some qualcomm platforms DPU needs to express a performance state
    requirement on a power domain depending on the clock rates.
    Use OPP table from DT to register with OPP framework and use
    dev_pm_opp_set_rate() to set the clk/perf state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds `dev_pm_opp_set_rate(dev, 0)` in `dpu_runtime_suspend` (line 1108) before calling `msm_dss_enable_clk(mp->clk_config, mp->num_clk, false)` to disable clocks. This ordering causes the voltage to drop to MIN_SVS while the core clock is still at a high frequency, creating a mismatch that can cause instability when the clock is re-enabled during resume. No fix is present; the vulnerable pattern is introduced.
